one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent misidentified the mystery binary as a Mandelbrot fractal renderer based solely on color gradient inspection, then spent the remainder of the trajectory in a fruitless loop of tweaking color constants rather than decompiling the binary to discover the actual ray-tracing algorithm.
t_err_evidence: Step 13: The agent writes mystery.c implementing a Mandelbrot fractal without any decompilation, acting on an unverified assumption that gradient colors (159,197,255) imply a Mandelbrot set; the analysis note confirms 'the binary appears to be a ray tracer producing a sky gradient and shaded geometry.'
t_commit_evidence: Step 20: After failing comparisons at steps 15/16/19 and making multiple tuning attempts, the agent explicitly continues adjusting Mandelbrot parameters (scale, iterations, color offsets) with no indication of switching to decompilation or a different algorithm; the trajectory is locked into the wrong model by this point.
t_surface_evidence: Step 15: diff -q reports 'Files original_image.ppm and image.ppm differ', providing a clear observable failure signal that the implementation does not match the binary's output.
trigger_explanation: At step 13 the agent acts on the unverified assumption that the gradient pixel values (159,197,255 transitioning to 67,67,67) uniquely indicate a Mandelbrot fractal. No decompilation (objdump, strings-based algorithm recovery, radare2) was attempted before committing to this algorithmic choice. The assumption was false — the binary implements a ray tracer.
forewarning_evidence: Step 15: 'Files original_image.ppm and image.ppm differ' is visible before t_commit=20. Steps 16, 19 also show concrete pixel mismatches (original 158,195,255 vs generated 159,197,255 or 156,193,255) providing repeated contradictory evidence before the outcome was locked in.
